paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU Pro confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics — Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy — on the MMLU Pro benchmark, as described in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.81 to 0.99 using a linear scale with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale with 0.2 increments. The blue solid line with circle markers represents “Final Accuracy,” which remains relatively high and stable across the confidence range, starting near 1.0 at 0.81, dipping slightly to ~0.92 at 0.82, then fluctuating narrowly between ~0.92 and 0.99 before ending near 1.0 at 0.99. The green dashed line with diamond markers shows “Initial Accuracy,” which begins at ~0.55 at 0.81, rises gradually with some fluctuations (e.g., ~0.65 at 0.85, ~0.75 at 0.87, ~0.78 at 0.90), and climbs more steeply toward the right, reaching ~0.95 at 0.99. The orange dash-dotted line with diamond markers indicates “Δ Accuracy,” which starts at ~0.45 at 0.81, declines to ~0.32 at 0.85, dips sharply to ~0.13 at 0.86, rises slightly to ~0.38 at 0.88, then falls again to ~0.12 at 0.90, and continues to decline overall, ending near 0.03 at 0.99. All lines include vertical error bars indicating variability, with larger error bars generally observed for Δ Accuracy, especially at lower confidence values.
